provenance.artifact: Linux Bedrock Dedicated Server 1.26.52.3 (bedrock_server, minecraft.net), run on our own machine with server-authoritative-movement-strict=true, player-position-acceptance-threshold=0.0001, online-mode=false; block replies read from its LevelEvent and UpdateBlock packets to a headless client
notes: r is read from LevelEvent 3600 (start cracking), whose data is floor(65535 · r); the break input from LevelEvent 2001; prediction answers from the UpdateBlock the server sent for the target in reply

hardness, tool speeds and harvest rules are the model's parameters: each was chosen to fit, and is accepted only because the model reproduces every 3600 value exactly; hardness_bracket is the range all cases allow

before each case the client was teleported to feet (60.5, 200, 0.5) on a stone floor at y 199, facing +z at pitch 36.75; it hit the north face of the block at (60, 200, 2) and sent the block actions listed per case in PlayerAuthInput, with input flag 35

where = water: the area was glass from (58, 199, -2) to (62, 203, 4), filled with water from (59, 200, -1) to (61, 202, 3) before the target was set; where = air: a stone block at (60, 202, 0) over the player's head and Levitation I; water+air: both

definition: r = s / (H · D) · M, the share of the block broken per input
s = the held tool's speed if the block lists the tool among suited_tools (tier speed, or 15 for shears and swords), else 1; plus L² + 1 for Efficiency L on a suited tool
D = 30 if the held item meets the block's harvest rule, else 100
M = (1 + 0.2·h) · 1.2^h for Haste level h (amplifier + 1; Conduit Power counts as Haste 1) × 0.21^f for Mining Fatigue level f × 1/5 with the eyes in water × 1/5 when not on the ground

N = ceil(1 / r); counting the start-break input as 0, the server breaks the block itself on input N − 1, and accepts a destroy prediction on input N − 1 but not before; it answers a rejected prediction by re-sending the block as it was
in creative, a start-break breaks the block on the same input, unless a sword is held

a break that is not stopped goes on after the block is gone: when water flows into the cell, crack updates for it follow (updates_after_break); a continue-destroy after the break starts cracking whatever fills the cell (starts_after_break)
